content_units: California Logo Project Contract Checklist

Use a short written agreement that clearly defines the project, payment timing, revision limits, ownership transfer, and change-order rules. For a fixed-price logo job in California, the main goal is to make scope, approvals, and fees easy to enforce.
Clause-by-Clause Contract Checklist
Clause   What to include   Brief sample wording

Parties and effective date   Legal names, business names, addresses or email contacts, and project start date of   2025-04-01     “This Agreement is entered into by and between [Designer Name] (‘Designer’) and [Client Name] (‘Client’) and is effective as of April 1, 2025.”

Project description   State that this is a fixed-price logo design project and identify the deliverables at a high level   “Designer will create one custom logo design package for Client on a fixed-fee basis, as described in this Agreement.”

Deliverables   List exactly what the client receives: logo concept(s), final approved logo, file formats, color versions, usage guide if included   “Final deliverables include the approved logo in AI, EPS, PDF, PNG, and JPG formats, in full-color, black, and white versions.”

Client content and inputs   Specify what the client must provide and when the timeline starts running   “Client will provide all required brand name, tagline, preferences, reference materials, and other content needed for the project. Delivery deadlines are measured from Designer’s receipt of all required content.”

Timeline and due date   Tie the schedule to content receipt; include the 14-day turnaround   “Designer will deliver the initial or final project deliverables, as applicable under the workflow, within fourteen (14) calendar days after receiving all required content and materials from Client.”

Revision rounds   State exactly   two revision rounds   and define what counts as a round   “The fee includes two (2) rounds of revisions to the selected logo direction. A revision round means one consolidated set of change requests submitted by Client after each review.”

Scope boundaries   Limit the work to logo design only unless separately priced   “This Agreement covers logo design only. Brand strategy, naming, copywriting, additional concepts, social media kits, business cards, brand guidelines, animation, or other collateral are not included unless added in writing.”

Change orders / scope creep protection   Require written approval and added fees for extra work   “Any request outside the agreed scope, including additional revision rounds or new deliverables, will be treated as additional services and billed only after written approval of a change order or email authorization.”

Fixed project fee   State the total flat fee and whether taxes or pass-through costs apply   “Client agrees to pay a fixed project fee of $[Amount] for the Services described in this Agreement. Any applicable taxes are the responsibility of [Client/Designer as required by law].”

Deposit and payment schedule   Include   50% upfront   and balance before release of final files   “A non-refundable advance payment equal to fifty percent (50%) of the project fee is due before work begins. The remaining fifty percent (50%) is due upon final approval and before release of editable or high-resolution final files.”

Late payment   Add due dates, interest/late fee if desired, and withholding of files until paid   “Amounts not paid when due may incur a late charge of $[flat fee] or [1–1.5%] per month, to the extent permitted by California law. Designer may withhold final files until all invoices are paid in full.”

Ownership and transfer of rights   Make clear that copyright transfers only after full payment; reserve portfolio rights if desired   “Designer retains all right, title, and interest, including copyright, in all work product until Client has paid all amounts due in full. Upon full payment, Designer assigns to Client the final approved logo files only, excluding preliminary concepts and unused drafts.”

Preliminary concepts and working files   Protect unused concepts and source files unless expressly included   “Unused concepts, sketches, drafts, and working files remain Designer’s property unless specifically listed as final deliverables.”

Portfolio and self-promotion   Reserve the right to display the work unless confidentiality prevents it   “Designer may display the work in portfolios, websites, social media, and promotional materials after the logo is publicly launched, unless the parties agree in writing to confidentiality restrictions.”

Client warranties   Client should confirm it has rights to materials it provides   “Client represents that it owns or has permission to use all text, images, trademarks, and other materials supplied to Designer and will indemnify Designer from claims arising from those materials.”

Originality / trademark disclaimer   Avoid guaranteeing trademark availability; recommend legal clearance   “Designer will create original work to the best of Designer’s knowledge, but does not provide trademark searches, legal opinions, or guarantees of trademark registrability or non-infringement. Client is responsible for legal clearance before use or registration.”

Approval process   Require prompt review and consolidated feedback   “Client will review each submission promptly and provide one consolidated response. Silence for more than [5–10] business days may delay the schedule.”

Kill fee / cancellation   Protect time already spent if the project stops midstream   “If Client cancels the project after work has begun, all amounts paid are retained, and Client will also pay for work completed beyond the deposit at Designer’s standard rate or a prorated portion of the fixed fee.”

No refund after start   Especially useful with a fixed-price creative project   “Because time is reserved and creative work begins immediately, fees paid are non-refundable once work has started, except as required by law.”
Independent contractor status   Clarify business relationship   “Designer is an independent contractor and not an employee, partner, or agent of Client.”

Limitation of liability   Cap exposure to the amount paid under the contract   “To the fullest extent allowed by law, Designer’s liability arising out of this Agreement will not exceed the total fees paid by Client under this Agreement.”

Dispute resolution and venue   Choose California law and county/venue; mediation first is common   “This Agreement is governed by California law. The parties agree to first attempt to resolve disputes through good-faith informal discussions and, if needed, mediation in [County], California, before filing suit, except for small claims or injunctive relief.”
Electronic signatures   Allow signing by email/PDF/e-sign   “Electronic signatures and scanned or emailed copies of this Agreement are deemed originals and fully enforceable.”
California-Specific Drafting Notes
Practical points for California
- California generally permits freelance design contracts like this, but contract terms must be clear, not unconscionable, and not contrary to state law.
- Avoid calling any charge a “penalty.” Use a reasonable   late fee   or interest clause instead.
- If you want a   non-refundable 50% upfront payment  , describe it as an advance retainer/deposit that reserves project time and covers commencement of work.
- Copyright ownership is governed by federal law, so the contract should clearly say transfer happens   only after full payment  .
- Do not promise trademark clearance unless you are actually providing that service.
Project context used here
- Start date:   2025-04-01
- Pricing model:   fixed-price
- Revisions included:   2 rounds
- Payment:   50% upfront, 50% before final file release
- Final files due:   within 14 days after receiving client content
- Priority:   prevent scope creep
